sources.citation: OLAC / SIL-PNG resource listings for Taupota [tpa] and Maiwala [mum] (the Internet Archive 2015, 2025-26 captures).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalog pages: for tpa only Nagai 1997, the 2001 Taupota Alphabet Development Worksheet (offline, SIL 70370), a 2001 trial spelling guide (SIL 70168), VITAL literacy books, Capell/PARADISEC wordlists; no OPD, grammar or phonology paper for Taupota exists in the listings.

sources.citation: McHenry, Marisa (ed.). 2013. Wedau (Topura dialect) Organised Phonology Data. SIL-PNG. 6 pp. (sister lect, wed)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Suprasegmentals section empty (and it is Wedau/Topura, not Taupota).

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study vol. 2, 441-523. Pacific Linguistics C-39.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Para 84 'STRESS' p.475, family-wide only: 'In all of the languages of PTC it seems that stress is predictable within certain word-classes, notably kinship nouns and verbs. When a kinship noun is pluralised by the addition of a suffix, the stress moves one syllable closer to the end of the word..'; phonemic stress named only for Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima (Nimowa, Sudest). Nothing Taupota-specific and no default position stated. Para 29 p.455 lists Taupota dialects (incl. Maiwala, Waiema).

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1907. The Melanesian languages of British New Guinea. In Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits vol. III: Linguistics, 413-503. Cambridge UP.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Taupota data (from Bishop of New Guinea / C. King MSS) used in comparative sound and grammar notes; no accent/stress statement for Taupota or Wedau.

sources.citation: Easton, Catherine. 2007. Discourses of orthography development: community-based practice in Milne Bay (P.N.G.). PhD thesis, La Trobe University. xii+305 pp. doi:10.26181/5fb5bf5e92b5f (open on La Trobe OPAL/figshare, file 25526708).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch.5 is a phonological description of the Wedau-to-Galuwahi chain with Taupota village as the type case (vowels, consonants, CV(m) syllables), but Sec.5.3 (printed p.121-122, PDF p.134) states 'I do not discuss stress for two reasons..' -- explicitly silent on stress placement; no stress marks in any transcription. Sec.8.2 (p.208-209) reports speakers saying Taupota differs from Wedau in 'tune' and stress patterns; fn.68 puts suprasegmentals beyond scope.
